clue.text: Thanks for publishing a good review

definitions.meaning: a favourable critical assessment of a work

explanation.surface: Someone expresses gratitude to a publisher for a positive write-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: gratitude expressed, and a sympathetic critical essay on an artist or work.

clue.text: Passionate admission by a right-winger

parts.note: the confession 'I am' is shortened to AM
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party, on the political right

explanation.surface: A conservative politician confesses to strong feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admission' gives AM, as in the admission 'I am'. TORY is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Amatory means relating to love or romantic desire, hence ardent.

clue.text: Quiet, dry couple

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction to play softly
to air laundry is to dry it out

explanation.surface: A reserved, deadpan pair of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is two of something, a twosome.

clue.text: I looked utterly disgusted on viewing it

definitions.text: I looked utterly disgusted on viewing it

parts.words: I looked utterly disgusted on viewing it
parts.note: describes something so ugly that anyone seeing it recoils; the start also plays on 'I' sounding like an organ of sight and 'disgusted' as aching

explanation.surface: Someone recounts recoiling in revulsion at a sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsightly thing offends anyone who looks at it, prompting disgust.

clue.text: Godless young devil clearly in debt

parts.note: an imp is a small or mischievous demon
someone visibly owing money holds IOUs, written promises to pay

explanation.surface: An irreligious youngster who is plainly broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking reverence for a deity is irreligious, without faith.

clue.text: Others take time to express hesitation

parts.note: to hem (as in hum and haw) is to make a hesitant noise

explanation.surface: Other people take a while to voice their uncertainty.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun for other people, as in 'us and them'.

clue.text: A personal favourite back in the dancehall

parts.note: one's is the possessive meaning belonging to a person

indicators.note: back tells us the word for a favourite is read from end to start

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Someone's favourite record makes a comeback at the dancehall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PET into TEP. The definition is loose: it points to something you would find in the dancehall, a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-step is a quick ballroom dance of the early twentieth century, performed in dancehalls.

clue.text: Obsession prior to getting a job

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
an occupation is a job or profession

explanation.surface: Someone's fixation in the days before landing work.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixation that fills the mind is a state of being engrossed.

clue.text: Becoming impassioned by the fire

parts.note: reads as growing emotional, but literally describes warming up beside a hearth

explanation.surface: Someone grows emotional while sitting beside the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing angry or excited is idiomatically warming up, and literally so beside flames.

clue.text: Understand that lies are out of order

indicators.note: out of order means these letters are jumbled and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Recognise that falsehoods are improper.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp a fact is to become aware of it, to comprehend.

clue.text: Go ahead and quietly withdraw

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction meaning softly
to recede is to move back or retreat

explanation.surface: An instruction to advance and then silently retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: To come before something is to lead it, going in front.

clue.text: Ex-pupil given old oriental instrument

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school
E stands for eastern

explanation.surface: A former student is handed an antique Eastern musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-reed woodwind of the orchestra is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Choose to attack

definitions.meaning: to assault, as in a dog that lunges at someone

explanation.surface: Deciding to launch an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to pick something and to set about someone violently.

clue.text: Most ethical writings contain printing order

indicators.note: the written words hold the answer inside them, running across the gap

explanation.surface: Highly moral texts include an instruction to the printer.
explanation.definitionFit: A proofreader's mark telling the printer to keep a deleted item, an instruction in typesetting.

clue.text: Points to animal shelter containing fabulous creature

parts.note: S and N are compass points, south and north
Noah's ark sheltered the animals from the flood

explanation.surface: Directions to a refuge that houses a mythical beast.
explanation.walkthrough: The ark is Noah's vessel that sheltered animals in the Bible story.
explanation.definitionFit: An imaginary animal invented by Lewis Carroll in a nonsense poem, hence fabled.

clue.text: Small cistern emitted a foul smell

parts.note: a cistern is a water tank

explanation.surface: A little water tank gave off a dreadful odour.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of a verb meaning to reek.

clue.text: Longing to tuck into sugar and pepper

indicators.note: tuck into means the word for longing is placed inside the word for sugar

parts.note: cane is sugar cane, a source of sugar
a yen is a craving or longing

explanation.surface: A craving to start on something sweet and spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuck into' looks like eating, but it puts YEN inside CANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot red spice ground from dried chillies is a kind of pepper.

clue.text: Organisation about to be attacked

parts.note: a set-up is an arrangement or organisation
on means about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A body that is on the verge of coming under assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To be assailed is to be set upon, a phrasal verb meaning assaulted.

clue.text: Each year syrup is used by a paper producer

parts.note: PA stands for per annum, Latin for each year

indicators.note: used here means worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Syrup is consumed annually by a papermaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian reed whose pith was pressed into early writing sheets is the plant that yields them.

clue.text: Saw a gypsy in the lead

indicators.note: in places the word for a wanderer within the symbol for the metal

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
a rover is a wanderer, like a travelling gypsy

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a traveller at the front of the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a past tense verb but is a noun meaning a saying; 'lead' is the metal, not first place.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim.

clue.text: Able to pay for a cleaning agent

definitions.meaning: having enough money to meet one's debts
a liquid that dissolves dirt or grease

explanation.surface: Being in funds to buy a cleaning product.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: financially sound, and a liquid that dissolves other substances.

clue.text: Sovereign about to enter parade

indicators.note: to enter means the word for about goes inside the word for parade

parts.note: a march is a procession or parade
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A ruler is on the point of joining a procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A king or queen who reigns is a sovereign ruler.

clue.text: Wonder if motoring club is within distance

indicators.note: is within means the club's letters sit inside the word for distance

parts.note: a mile is a measure of distance
the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: Someone ponders whether the motoring club is close by.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is a British breakdown and motoring organisation, like the AA.
explanation.definitionFit: A marvel or extraordinary event is a wonder.

clue.text: Dicky was hit by a car

definitions.meaning: British slang for unwell or weak, as in a dicky heart

explanation.surface: Someone poorly after being struck by a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: exhausted and in poor health, and knocked down by a vehicle.

clue.text: Excessively large implement

parts.note: too means excessively, as in too hot

explanation.surface: An oversized piece of equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool is an implement or instrument used for work.

clue.text: Look furious when left in a French station

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the French word for a station

parts.note: gare is French for a railway station

explanation.surface: Someone scowls angrily on being abandoned at a station in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like abandoned, but it is L.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare angrily is to glower fiercely.

clue.text: Reflective articles written by a woman

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: reflective means a mirror image, so a copy of the article is read backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Thoughtful essays penned by a female writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' gives AN twice: one stays as AN, and 'Reflective' turns the other into NA.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female given name, so a woman.

clue.text: Only 51

parts.note: fifty is L in Roman numerals, and the one is spelt out
fifty is L in Roman numerals, and the one is spelt out

explanation.surface: A bare number, just fifty-one.
explanation.walkthrough: 51 splits into fifty (Roman L) and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary, single, the sole one.

clue.text: Duty means nothing to student body

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
the NUS is the National Union of Students, a British student body

explanation.surface: Obligation counts for nothing to the student union.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUS is Britain's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or responsibility one must bear.

clue.text: Industrious Cockney's aspiration soared

parts.note: an aspiration is a hope; a Cockney drops the H
rose means went up, soared

explanation.surface: A hard-working Londoner's hopes climbed high.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys (working-class Londoners) traditionally drop the initial H. 'Aspiration' also hints at the breathed H that goes missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare word meaning laborious or busy, from the Latin for work.

clue.text: Organists play it to offer comfort

definitions.meaning: the desk of keyboards and stops at which an organ is played

explanation.surface: Organ players perform to soothe their listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an organ's keyboard desk, and to comfort someone grieving.

clue.text: Warning of instruction about accusative case

indicators.note: about places the word for instruction after its subject, a lesson concerning something

parts.note: the accusative is the objective case in grammar
a lesson is a period of instruction

explanation.surface: Grammar teaching on the accusative serves as a caution.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical example that teaches by cautionary example, a salutary warning.
